clauses.text: A foreign protocol command is refused with a typed FOREIGN_PROTOCOL_COMMAND that names the protocol owner, the full invocation and the route to run instead, and is never refused as a bare unknown command.
The refusal names the owning protocol, the exact requested command, and carries next_action guidance, so the caller cannot read it as a typo.
SAIPEN verbs and shortcuts (cc, continue, next, status) remain SAIPEN-owned and unaffected by foreign-protocol routing.
A malformed or absent exact_namespace block degrades to the old refusal without inventing an owner.
The router and registry suites are unaffected by the exact-namespace declaration.

Never present a foreign protocol as a candidate for an explicit SAIPEN command; an explicit /saipen <cmd> must never be dispatched to a skill whose name merely resembles it, and exact namespace ownership is decided before semantic skill matching.
A NO_HOME or similar refusal from a foreign protocol must not trigger a working-directory change into another protocol repository, a sibling-repo search, or the creation of that protocol home.
Re-read the installed skills directory on session start so a stale inventory cannot map a namespace to the wrong owner.
The FreeBuff host stops offering a substitute protocol for an explicit SAIPEN command.
A live /saipen continue in _BZ_REA on FreeBuff executes the SAIPEN route end to end.
Foreign-protocol side effects are reconciled by their owner through canonical append-only operations, preserving chronology and provenance, with no rewrite and no deletion.
No native pre-render interception is claimed for a host that declares response enforcement ADVISORY and pre-output interception NONE.
SAIPAL recognition is not authorization: a model-supplied witness is never upgraded to an authenticated operator-origin event.
